events.headline: ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya in Landmark, Final Judgment
events.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled 9-6 on Nov 19 that Myanmar's military and state organs committed genocide against the Rohingya in Rakhine State starting in 2017 — the first-ever ICJ state-genocide finding. The non-appealable ruling orders Myanmar to ensure safe Rohingya return, property restitution and rehabilitation support.

events.headline: US and Venezuela Sign Military Partnership Deal as Hegseth Visits Caracas
events.summary: US Defense Secretary Hegseth signed an agreement with acting President Delcy Rodríguez covering joint training, intelligence sharing, and counter-narcotics cooperation. Hegseth called Venezuela a 'compliant security partner' during the Caracas visit.

events.headline: China Deploys 100+ Vessels in Unannounced 'Silent' Naval Drills Around Taiwan
events.summary: Taiwanese officials observed China deploying over 100 PLA Navy and coast guard vessels, including carriers Liaoning and Fujian, across the First Island Chain in an unannounced exercise larger than 2025's 'Justice Mission' drill. Analysts described it as 'silent intimidation' simulating an isolation or blockade scenario.

events.headline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Nears 11,800 Cases, 5,700 Deaths, Deadliest on Record
events.summary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has grown to nearly 11,800 cases and more than 5,700 deaths, making it the deadliest on record, with North Kivu now accounting for 40% of new cases. The WHO chief has called for peace amid heavy fighting that continues to disrupt the response in the epicenter region.

events.headline: Crimean Bridge Rail Traffic Halted After Third Ukrainian Strike; Span Collapse Confirmed
events.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed Neptune missiles struck the Crimean Bridge's rail section just after midnight on November 19, halting train traffic in the third strike in a week. Satellite imagery shows a collapsed span of the road bridge's main arch, with the strikes preceding Putin's meeting with Xi and Trump and Russia's retaliatory strikes on Kyiv.

events.headline: Mamdani Unveils Plan to Close Rikers Island, Delays Deadline to 2032
events.summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani released the city's first comprehensive plan to close Rikers Island, proposing four new borough-based jails (Brooklyn opening 2029, Bronx/Queens 2031, Manhattan 2032) and pushing the legally mandated 2027 closure deadline to 2032. The plan includes $50 million for job training, mental health counseling, and drug treatment, and requires legislative approval.

events.headline: Houthi Drone Attack Wounds 11 at Riyadh's PIF Tower, Second Strike This Month
events.summary: A Houthi drone attack wounded 11 people at Riyadh's PIF Tower, marking the second such strike on the Saudi capital region this month. The Saudi-led coalition condemned the attack as a terrorist act amid rising cross-border drone and missile activity from Yemen.

events.headline: Washington Governor Condemns 'Out of Control' ICE Operation at SeaTac Airport
events.summary: Masked ICE agents detained two passengers, reportedly including a minor, as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight at Sea-Tac Airport on Saturday morning. The Port of Seattle and Alaska Airlines said they had no advance notice; Gov. Bob Ferguson called ICE 'completely and totally out of control.'

events.headline: Pennsylvania Confirms Ninth Measles Death as Outbreak Reaches 1,638 Cases
events.summary: Pennsylvania health officials confirmed on Nov. 23 that an unvaccinated Centre County resident died of measles, the state's ninth measles-associated death of 2026, with confirmed cases reaching 1,638 across 46 counties and 330 hospitalizations. Deaths have now occurred in six counties; the news follows the CDC's confirmation that the U.S. lost its 25-year measles elimination status.

events.headline: Russia's Novaya Gazeta Newspaper Closes Moscow Office Amid 'Foreign Agent' Crackdown
events.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's last major independent newspapers, closed its Moscow office after being designated a 'foreign agent,' fined, blocked online, and cut off from donation-based funding. The UN human rights chief called it another devastating blow to independent media in Russia.

events.headline: Jury Convicts Jonathan Rinderknecht of Starting Deadly Palisades Fire
events.summary: A federal jury convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, on Nov. 20 of destruction of property by fire and arson affecting interstate commerce for igniting the Jan. 1, 2025 'Lachman Fire,' which grew into the Palisades Fire. The conviction came in a retrial after an earlier mistrial; sentencing is pending, with each count carrying 5 to 20 years.

events.headline: Russian 'Double-Tap' Strike on Zelensky's Hometown Kryvyi Rih Kills Child, Injures Over 70
events.summary: A Russian ballistic missile and drone strike on Kryvyi Rih on Nov 20 killed a 7-year-old boy and a paramedic, with follow-up drone strikes hitting rescuers. The injury toll rose to about 73, including nine children, and roughly two dozen apartment buildings plus a hospital were damaged.

events.headline: Russia Strikes Three Kyiv Dnipro Bridges in Biggest River-Crossing Attack of the War
events.summary: Overnight on November 20, Russian ballistic missiles and drones struck three bridges spanning Kyiv's Dnipro River as part of a barrage of over 100 missiles and 400 drones nationwide, killing at least 3-6 people and wounding 15-28. It is described as the largest attack on Kyiv's river crossings since the war began, following Ukraine's third Crimean Bridge strike and Putin's vow of retaliation.

events.headline: COP31 Climate Talks Collapse in Antalya Over Fossil Fuel Language
events.summary: UN climate negotiations at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, broke down after countries failed to agree on fossil fuel phase-out language, with observers calling it the 'worst COP ever.' The collapse leaves major gaps in global climate policy ahead of 2027.

events.headline: EU Proposes 22nd Sanctions Package Targeting Russian Banks, Soldiers and Athletes
events.summary: The European Commission proposed its 22nd sanctions package against Russia, targeting banks, military personnel and including a proposed ban on Russian athletes from international sporting events. The package reflects continued EU efforts to pressure Moscow over the war in Ukraine.

events.headline: Virginia Reports First Measles-Associated Death of 2026
events.summary: A child under age 4 died from measles, Virginia's first measles death since 1978, part of a national outbreak that has killed at least 12 in the US in 2026. Virginia has logged 220 confirmed cases this year, 41 since October 17, almost entirely among unvaccinated people.

events.headline: Virginia Regulators Hold Evidentiary Hearings on $67 Billion Dominion-NextEra Merger
events.summary: The Virginia State Corporation Commission held three days of evidentiary hearings starting November 17 on the proposed $67 billion merger of Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy, with roughly 30 intervening parties. SCC staff has already recommended rejecting the merger as structured, and a final ruling is due by January 11, 2027.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Syzran and Kuibyshev Refineries in Russia's Samara Region
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Syzran and Kuibyshev oil refineries in Russia's Samara Oblast, setting them ablaze and reportedly cutting Russia's refining capacity by roughly a third. The strikes are part of Kyiv's intensified campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.

events.headline: Ukrainian Naval Drones Sink Russian Corvette Merkury at Benghazi, Libya
events.summary: Ukrainian naval drones struck and reportedly sank the Russian corvette Merkury at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya. The strike extends Ukraine's long-range maritime drone campaign against Russian naval assets far beyond the Black Sea.

events.headline: Sinaloa Cartel Violence Continues in Mexico After 'El Chapo Isidro' Capture
events.summary: Fallout continues in Sinaloa state after Mexican forces captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro,' in a raid near Guasave that sparked a firefight killing 11 people. The capture, confirmed by the US Justice Department, targeted one of the FBI's ten most-wanted fugitives.

events.headline: Trump Withholds Authorization for Joint Israel-US Strike on Iran
events.summary: US President Trump declined to authorize a joint Israel-US strike on Iran despite pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu before Israel's election. Separately, a reported blast on Iran's Qeshm Island was attributed to routine munitions disposal rather than a military strike.

events.headline: Iran Strike Wounds Two on Bahrain's Sitra Island; IRGC Claims Patriot Radar Hit
events.summary: An Iranian strike wounded two people at an industrial site on Bahrain's Sitra Island, with Iran's IRGC claiming it hit a Patriot missile defense radar. Saudi Arabia condemned the attack as part of an escalating pattern of Iranian strikes across the Gulf.

events.headline: Oregon Joins Virginia in Suing SpaceX Over Grok AI's Sexualized Deepfakes of Minors
events.summary: Oregon's attorney general filed suit in Multnomah County Circuit Court on Nov. 23, coordinated with Virginia's lawsuit, alleging Grok's 'Spicy' mode let users turn AI images into sexualized video clips without consent, including of minors. The suit cites a study estimating Grok produced 1.8-3 million sexualized images, about 23,000 appearing to depict children; Oregon and Virginia are the first states to sue SpaceX since its xAI acquisition.

events.headline: Russian Drone Again Violates Polish Airspace Near Dorohusk; Ambassador Summoned
events.summary: A Russian drone violated Polish airspace near Dorohusk for roughly nine minutes, the second such breach in days, prompting Poland to summon Russia's ambassador and convene a NATO council meeting. The repeated incursions have heightened alarm about Russian provocations along NATO's eastern flank.

events.headline: Egypt Presses Hamas on Gaza Weapons Handover Under 15-Point Roadmap
events.summary: Egypt is pressing Hamas to honor commitments on a Gaza weapons handover under a 15-point roadmap, as Palestinian factions continue stabilization talks in Cairo. Hamas says it remains committed to the deal while a proposed Board of Peace weighs a new plan.

events.headline: Asia-Pacific Stocks Rally After Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
events.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he resigned amid a scandal, triggering a sharp Asia-Pacific stock rally. KOSPI jumped roughly 7.5%, the Nikkei gained 4.5%, and Taiwan's Taiex surged 9.1% as the AI-chip trade rebounded sharply from its prior slump.

events.headline: Indonesian Candy Factory Fire Toll Rises to 24 Confirmed Dead, Dozens Missing
events.summary: The death toll from a fire at a candy factory in Cikande, Banten, Indonesia, has risen to at least 24 confirmed dead, with dozens still unaccounted for and the toll possibly rising to 26. Rescuers continue searching the site for missing workers.

events.headline: Supercell Storm Kills Up to 5, Damages 5,000 Homes in Tupanciretã, Brazil
events.summary: A rare supercell storm with winds up to 114 km/h struck Tupanciretã in Rio Grande do Sul, killing 3-5 people and injuring dozens to hundreds. Around 5,000 homes were damaged and the state declared a calamity.

events.headline: Eighth Circuit Clears Army to Detonate Toxic Lead Compound at Iowa Ammunition Plant
events.summary: The Eighth Circuit lifted a court stay around Nov. 23-24, clearing the Army to proceed with controlled detonations of about 10,000 lbs of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, planned for Nov. 25, despite a prior Trump directive pausing the plan pending appellate review. Environmental groups warn the resulting lead-dust plume could reach communities up to 100 miles away.

events.headline: Al-Shabaab Ambushes Somali Forces in Two Lower Shabelle Incidents, Casualty Tolls Disputed
events.summary: Al-Shabaab fighters ambushed Somali military convoys in separate incidents near Yaqbirweyne and Jame'o in Lower Shabelle/Bay regions, with casualty figures sharply disputed between the group and Somali officials. Somalia's military claims to have killed militants including commanders in response, and the president ordered a military-court investigation into one ambush.

events.headline: EU and UK Finalize Post-Brexit 'Reset' Deal at Brussels Summit
events.summary: The EU and UK concluded a summit agreement to remove plant and animal export checks, link carbon trading systems, and create a capped Youth Experience Scheme for ages 18-31. UK PM Andy Burnham's office estimates the deal could add about 0.5% to GDP, worth roughly £17 billion.

events.headline: FEMA's $400M Florida Disaster Aid Leaves Brevard County Flood Recovery in Limbo
events.summary: More than three weeks after record flooding along the St. Johns River near Cocoa, FEMA announced on Nov. 23 nearly $400 million for 144 Florida disaster-recovery projects, but the award covers prior disasters and does not include approval of Florida's pending Nov. 9 request for aid tied to this month's Brevard County flooding. Florida has completed roughly 500 floodwater rescues; Melbourne and Palm Bay are on pace for their wettest year on record.

events.headline: Guyana Rejects Bilateral Talks After US Official Floated Ceding Essequibo Land to Venezuela
events.summary: Reuters reported a departing US State Department official floated allowing Venezuela partial control of Guyana's Essequibo region. Guyana rejected bilateral negotiations, insisting the territorial dispute be resolved via the ICJ, while the State Department said policy remains unchanged.

events.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea Continue Drone and Artillery Exchanges Near Badme
events.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea continue to mass forces and exchange drone and artillery fire near the disputed town of Badme, prompting civilians to flee the border area. The buildup has heightened fears of a broader resumption of war between the two countries.

events.headline: Guatemala's 30-Day State of Siege Continues in Zacapa and Izabal Amid Cartel Violence
events.summary: Guatemala's state of siege in Zacapa and Izabal, declared after an ambush killed a congressman and three police officers, remains in effect through mid-December. A related attack killed five more officers, and the US designated three cartel-linked clans as terrorist organizations, raising concerns ahead of 2027 elections.

events.headline: Russian Helicopter and Jet-Powered Drone Breach Finnish and Moldovan Airspace in Same Wave
events.summary: Finland's defense ministry said a Russian helicopter penetrated about 4km into its airspace near Loviisa, hours after a drone strike set fire to the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland. The same night, a jet-powered drone crossed into Moldovan airspace near Troitske/Purcari twice during a Russian attack on Ukraine; Norway condemned both violations.

events.headline: Hawaii Lawmakers Plan Hearing Into Delayed Disclosure of H-POWER Diesel Spill, Rare Plant Sanctuary Impact
events.summary: Hawaii House Speaker Nadine Nakamura and Senate committee chair Carol Fukunaga are planning a formal hearing into why officials waited months after detecting a roughly 400,000-gallon diesel leak near the H-POWER plant before disclosing it publicly in mid-November. Civil Beat reports the spill, first detected in May and fully scoped by July, reached the Kipuka o Kahinahina sanctuary for the endangered 'Ewa Hinahina plant.

events.headline: RSF Accused of Executing Captured Soldiers as It Seizes More Blue Nile Territory
events.summary: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces are accused of executing captured army prisoners near Dinring as the RSF-SPLM-N alliance seized Bau and seven other areas in Blue Nile state. The advance brings the paramilitary coalition closer to the state capital Ed Damazin.

events.headline: Drone Attacks Hit Colombian Police Bases in Cúcuta and Curumaní, Injuring Civilians
events.summary: Explosive drone attacks struck police bases in Cúcuta and Curumaní in Colombia's Catatumbo/Cesar border region, injuring civilians including an infant and damaging about 60 homes. A police officer was also injured in Curumaní. The attacks are part of an escalating pattern of armed-group drone strikes in the area.

events.headline: Three Salvadoran Soldiers Killed in Explosives Accident During Haiti Deployment
events.summary: Three Salvadoran soldiers were killed and two injured in an accidental explosion while handling explosives during El Salvador's military anti-gang deployment in Haiti. They are the first fatalities of the roughly 2,000-2,500 troop deployment that began October 18, 2026.

events.headline: Michigan Measles Outbreak Grows in Hillsdale and St. Joseph Counties
events.summary: The Branch-Hillsdale-St. Joseph Community Health Agency confirmed a new measles outbreak on Nov. 17, with 12 cases split evenly between Hillsdale and St. Joseph counties. Statewide, Michigan has reached roughly 30 confirmed cases in 2026 across 14 separate outbreaks amid a national measles resurgence after the CDC confirmed the U.S. lost its elimination status.

events.headline: Witness Calls Texas Execution of Reinaldo Dennes 'Botched'; State Disputes Claim
events.summary: Reinaldo Dennes was executed Nov. 19 for a 1996 Houston robbery-murder, but his spiritual adviser, Rev. Jeff Hood, said technicians struggled for about an hour to find a vein and that Dennes screamed during the procedure, calling it 'unquestionably botched.' The Texas Department of Criminal Justice disputes the characterization and says protocol was followed; an AP witness described it as 'dramatically different' from past executions.

events.headline: US Investigates Possible Iranian Cyberattacks on Up to 50 Gulf Shipping Vessels
events.summary: US officials are investigating whether Iran is behind a wave of cyberattacks affecting up to 50 commercial vessels in Gulf shipping lanes, exploiting Fortinet networking-equipment vulnerabilities. Russia is also being considered as a possible source of the campaign.
events.locationName: Persian Gulf (via Dubai), United Arab Emirates

events.headline: Hungarian PM Magyar Meets Zelensky in Uzhhorod, Breaking With Orbán-Era Stance
events.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar met Ukrainian President Zelensky in Uzhhorod, his first visit to Ukraine since 2015 and a sharp break from the previous Orbán government's approach. The meeting signals a potential shift in Hungary's posture toward Kyiv.

events.headline: China-Linked Disinformation and Russian Aircraft Activity Precede Taiwan's Taipei Vote
events.summary: A China-linked disinformation campaign and increased Russian aircraft activity have emerged ahead of Taiwan's November 28 Taipei mayoral election. Analysts say Beijing has taken a strong interest in the local race despite officials downplaying its cross-strait significance.

events.headline: Saudi Arabia's Economy Contracts 3.8% in Q3 2026 on Oil-Sector Slump
events.summary: Saudi Arabia's GASTAT data showed real GDP fell 3.8% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, an improvement from a 4.7% contraction in Q2, driven by a 20.4% drop in oil-sector activity linked to Iran war and Houthi-related disruptions. Non-oil GDP grew about 1.9-2%, while oil revenue fell 23% year-on-year.

events.headline: South Korea's Ruling Party Formalizes Push to Impeach Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae
events.summary: After the Supreme Court partly overturned ex-PM Han Duck-soo's martial-law conviction, South Korea's ruling Democratic Party adopted impeachment of Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae as official policy, calling the ruling 'historic treason.' The party plans to file the motion around Dec 3 and seeks a floor vote by year-end, while opposition party PPP calls it an 'assembly coup.'

events.headline: Cyclone Xavier Weakens to Category 1 as Relief Reaches Cook Islands
events.summary: Severe Tropical Cyclone Xavier, which peaked at Category 5 over the northern Cook Islands, weakened to Category 1 by Nov 21. New Zealand's Air Force delivered over five tonnes of relief supplies to Rarotonga for onward shipment, with a barge to Pukapuka and Nassau scheduled for Nov 23.

events.headline: Marana, Arizona Approves Business License for ICE Detention Center Amid Abuse Concerns
events.summary: The Marana Town Council voted Nov. 18 to approve a $60 business license for Management & Training Corporation to operate a 775-bed ICE detention facility in a former state prison. The approval came despite unresolved discrepancies in a 2023 federal audit regarding sexual-abuse reporting, drawing criticism from advocacy group PRICE.

events.headline: Car Bomb Wounds Over 20 in Villavicencio, Colombia; FARC Dissidents Blamed
events.summary: A car bomb detonated in Villavicencio, Meta department, Colombia, wounding between 23 and 25 people. Authorities blame FARC dissident factions for the attack amid ongoing insurgent violence in the region.

events.headline: Russian Strikes Kill Two in Odesa Region as Dozens Remain Trapped on Kinburn Spit
events.summary: Russian strikes on Odesa Oblast killed two people, including a 17-year-old boy, and injured three more, while separate strikes injured two in Kyiv. Roughly 100 people remain trapped on the Russian-occupied Kinburn Spit amid continued damage to the region's power grid.

events.headline: Cuba Accuses US of Trying to 'Impose Peace Through Force' Amid Trump Threats
events.summary: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez accused the United States of seeking to impose peace through force, after President Trump said he wanted to resolve the Cuba situation before leaving office and floated a possible brief military operation against the island.

events.headline: Near-Record King Tides and Storm Threaten San Francisco Bay Area Coast
events.summary: A storm colliding with seasonal king tides is forecast to push San Francisco Bay water levels to roughly 8.6-11.5 feet around Nov. 25, approaching or exceeding the 1983 record. Forecasters warn of 15-20 ft breaking waves and 40-50 mph winds, with flooding risk to SFO and the Embarcadero; Mayor Daniel Lurie called the threat 'extremely serious.'

events.headline: Israeli Airstrike Kills Hamas Internal Security Chief in Gaza City
events.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed Hamas internal security chief Naeem Abu Nahel and six other Palestinians in Gaza City's Shati area. The strike comes as Palestinian factions hold talks in Cairo on a proposed Gaza stabilization force protocol.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Intensifies Airstrikes in Shan and Rakhine States, Killing Civilians
events.summary: Myanmar's junta intensified airstrikes in Mongmit township in Shan State, where human shields were reportedly used, as well as in Ponnagyun and Pauktaw in Rakhine State, killing dozens of civilians. The escalation comes as ASEAN leaders meet to discuss the country's ongoing civil conflict.

events.headline: Montana Judge Blocks Enforcement of Law Defining Sex as Strictly Binary
events.summary: A Missoula County District Court judge granted a preliminary injunction blocking enforcement of Senate Bill 437, a 2025 Montana law defining sex strictly by reproductive biology, finding transgender, intersex, and Two Spirit plaintiffs likely to succeed on state constitutional privacy and equal-protection claims. The law remains blocked while litigation continues; the state plans to appeal.

events.headline: Pennsylvania Revokes Sharon Regional Medical Center's License, Forces Hospital Closure
events.summary: Pennsylvania's Department of Health revoked Sharon Regional Medical Center's operating license on Nov. 4, effective Nov. 17, after its electricity provider moved to cut power over unpaid bills. Gov. Josh Shapiro's office accused owner Tenor Health Foundation of mismanagement; inpatient care had already paused in late October.

events.headline: Natural Gas Pipeline Fire Lights Up Night Sky Over West Alabama, No Injuries Reported
events.summary: A Southern Natural Gas Company pipeline released gas and ignited near Ward in Sumter County around 11:27 p.m. Saturday, sending flames over 100 feet high that were visible 50-60 miles away in Alabama and Mississippi. No injuries or structure damage were reported; the line was shut and depressurized, residents were briefly evacuated, and the cause is under investigation.

events.headline: Ohio Gun Bill Loosening Suppressor and Vehicle-Carry Rules Awaits DeWine's Signature
events.summary: Ohio's legislature passed SB 278, the 'Freedom to Carry Act,' which removes short-barreled rifles, shotguns and suppressors from the state's 'dangerous ordnance' list, lowers the permitless concealed-carry age from 21 to 18, and ends the secured-compartment requirement for carrying firearms in vehicles and boats. The bill now awaits Gov. Mike DeWine's signature; his office says it is weighing law-enforcement concerns.

events.headline: Arizona Regulators Approve Nearly 10% Rate Hike for Tucson Electric Power
events.summary: The outgoing Arizona Corporation Commission voted 4-1 on Nov. 17-18 to approve a roughly 9.4% rate increase for Tucson Electric Power customers, adding about $13 a month, effective Dec. 1. The commission also approved a new formula-rate mechanism opposed by the state attorney general's office; Commissioner Lea Marquez Peterson dissented.

events.headline: UK Warns Defence Suppliers to Ukraine of Russian Sabotage Risk
events.summary: British security services warned UK defence suppliers to Ukraine that they face a heightened risk of Russian sabotage. The warning reflects growing concern over covert Russian operations targeting Western military supply chains.

events.headline: Australia and Solomon Islands Sign Security Pact, Dropping 2022 China Deal
events.summary: Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a major new security pact, with Honiara dropping its 2022 security agreement with China. The deal strengthens Australia's strategic position in the Pacific amid ongoing competition with Beijing for regional influence.

events.headline: Gas Explosion at Hanoi Hot Pot Restaurant Kills Six, Injures Over 14
events.summary: A suspected gas explosion at a hot pot restaurant in Hanoi's Dong Da Ward killed six people and injured more than 14 others. Vietnamese authorities are investigating the cause of the blast.

events.headline: RSF Drone Strikes Kill Four in Khartoum, Damage UN Building
events.summary: Drone attacks blamed on Sudan's Rapid Support Forces killed four people in and around Khartoum and damaged a UN building, the first such strike on UN premises since the army retook the capital in May 2025. Sudan's army separately accused the RSF of executing captured soldiers near Dinring, Blue Nile, an allegation that remains unverified.

events.headline: Merz Rejects 'Yalta-Style' Ukraine Deal Without Kyiv at Berlin Coalition Summit
events.summary: At a 'Coalition of the Willing' summit in Berlin, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz rejected any great-power deal on Ukraine struck without Kyiv and Europe, saying a Yalta-style format will not bring peace. His remarks followed a Trump-Putin-Xi summit that produced a Ukraine statement without naming the country.

events.headline: Somalia Expels UAE Ambassador Over Alleged Unauthorized Military Bases
events.summary: Somalia expelled the UAE ambassador and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, accusing the UAE of operating unauthorized military bases in Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo, calling it an 'open invasion.' The UAE called the move escalatory and hostile and rejected the accusations.

events.headline: NYC Council Grills FDNY as Lithium-Ion Battery Fires Hit Record High
events.summary: Following fatal battery fires in Brooklyn and the Bronx that killed ten people, the NYC Council held an emergency hearing on Nov. 20 questioning the FDNY over a record 406 lithium-ion battery fires so far in 2026, up from 241 over the same period in 2025. Citywide fire deaths have risen to 90 this year from 51 last year, and the Council is weighing seven battery-safety bills.

events.headline: Georgia Democrats Win Control of State House for First Time in Two Decades
events.summary: Following certification of Georgia's midterm results, Democrats secured the 91 seats needed for a majority in the 180-member state House, flipping control for the first time in roughly two decades. Minority Leader Carolyn Hugley is positioned to become the chamber's first Black woman speaker, while Republicans retained the state Senate majority.

events.headline: Pentagon Restricts Aspects of US-Canada Military Cooperation, Report Says
events.summary: The Washington Post reported that US Defense Secretary Hegseth issued a classified directive restricting some US-Canada military cooperation, including joint exercises, training, and defense planning. NORAD operations, intelligence-sharing, and NATO commitments are excluded, and Canada's defense minister said no operational change has been detected.

events.headline: Federal Judge Permanently Bars California From Enforcing Mask-Ban Law Against ICE Agents
events.summary: U.S. District Judge Christina Snyder entered a permanent injunction barring California from enforcing its 'No Vigilantes Act' and 'No Secret Police Act' facial-covering and visible-ID requirements against federal agents, including ICE. The ruling followed a joint stipulation between the Justice Department and California, dismissing DOJ's year-old lawsuit; state lawmakers are reportedly drafting a revised bill, SB 1004.

events.headline: Amtrak Sunset Limited Derails After Striking Truck Hauling Bulldozer in Louisiana
events.summary: An Amtrak Sunset Limited train carrying about 95 passengers struck an 18-wheeler stuck on the tracks at a grade crossing near Broussard around 6:05 p.m. Sunday, derailing its locomotives and lead baggage cars. Four to five passengers were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries.

events.headline: Two COTA Bus Drivers Killed in Head-On Crash in Columbus
events.summary: Two Central Ohio Transit Authority buses collided head-on during morning rush hour on Nov. 23 after one bus crossed the center line and struck a stopped bus, which was pushed into an SUV and a sedan. Both drivers, longtime COTA employees, died, and nine riders and occupants were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries; the cause is under investigation.

events.headline: Argentina's Peso and Country Risk Hit 12-Month Lows Amid Economic Contraction
events.summary: Argentina's peso and country-risk spread hit 12-month lows amid a bond selloff and election uncertainty, with September economic activity contracting 1.2% year-on-year. The downturn adds pressure on the government's fiscal and monetary stabilization plans.

events.headline: Mass Protests Continue in France and Germany Over Cost of Living, Conscription
events.summary: France saw its sixth consecutive weekend of protests over the cost of living and public services, while Germany experienced demonstrations against conscription plans that included rioting and looting in Frankfurt. The unrest reflects growing public discontent with economic and security policies across Western Europe.

events.headline: Russian Strike Partially Destroys Apartment Block in Zaporizhzhia, Killing Two
events.summary: A Russian strike partially destroyed a five-story apartment block in the Kosmichnyi district of Zaporizhzhia overnight, killing two people and injuring 22 others, including two children. Rescue operations continued through the following day.

events.headline: Gunmen Ambush Nigerian Senate Candidate Omo-Agege's Convoy, Killing Four
events.summary: Gunmen attacked the campaign convoy of Senate candidate and former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege in Uduere, Delta State, killing four people including two aides and wounding four others. His campaign alleges a targeted assassination attempt, and a curfew was imposed.

events.headline: Sudanese Army Intensifies Airstrikes on RSF Positions in Nyala, South Darfur
events.summary: Sudanese army aircraft and drones intensified strikes on RSF headquarters and positions in Nyala, South Darfur's capital, killing and wounding paramilitary fighters including an officer. The strikes are part of a weeks-long aerial campaign to degrade RSF capability ahead of a possible ground assault.

events.headline: Russian Drone Strike Destroys Apartment Block in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast, Killing at Least 10
events.summary: A Russian strike drone destroyed a section of a five-story residential building in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast overnight. The confirmed death toll rose to at least 10 by Nov 23, with search operations continuing; a kindergarten and shop were also damaged.

events.headline: Pennsylvania Senate Democrats Secure First Majority in Three Decades
events.summary: Following Nov. 3 midterm elections, Pennsylvania Democrats flipped control of the state Senate to a 26-24 majority for the first time in roughly 30 years, giving the party a full trifecta with the governorship and House for the first time since 1993. Key flips included Mark Pinsley and Chris Thomas unseating GOP incumbents, opening a path for stalled legislation.

events.headline: Fourth Circuit Gives Virginia Mixed Ruling on ICE Cooperation and Mask Laws
events.summary: On Nov. 23, a Fourth Circuit panel ruled Virginia may restrict localities from cooperating with ICE under 287(g) agreements without violating the Contracts Clause, but kept blocked a separate provision requiring ICE agents to unmask and show identification, finding it violates intergovernmental immunity. Circuit Judge Robert King dissented on the mask-ban ruling.

events.headline: Three People Found Dead in West Virginia Shooting, Suspect at Large
events.summary: West Virginia State Police and Jefferson County deputies responding to a shooting call in Kearneysville around 6:25 p.m. on Nov. 23 found three people dead from gunshot wounds inside a home. The suspect fled before police arrived, and as of Nov. 24 an extensive multi-agency search was ongoing with no identities released.

events.headline: Utah Certifies Election Results, Confirming Democrats Broke GOP House Supermajority
events.summary: Utah's State Board of Canvassers voted unanimously on Nov. 23 to certify 2026 election results, confirming Democrats and two unaffiliated candidates flipped 16 Republican-held House seats, nearly doubling the Democratic caucus and ending Republicans' veto-proof supermajority for the first time in over three decades. Republicans retain overall control of both chambers; Gov. Spencer Cox called it a 'historic defeat.'

events.headline: Armenia Proposes New Constitution in Peace Bid With Azerbaijan Amid Border Blast
events.summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan proposed a new draft constitution as part of efforts to finalize peace with Azerbaijan, while Georgia's foreign minister visited Baku to support the process. Separately, a landmine explosion in Azerbaijan's Aghstafa region killed one person and seriously injured another.

events.headline: Gunmen Hold Dozens Hostage at Cartagena Supermarket After Botched Robbery
events.summary: Armed robbers who failed to steal a cash truck took refuge in a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, holding roughly 25 people hostage. Police surrounded the building as negotiations continued.

events.headline: El Niño Flooding Kills 27 in Ecuador, Triggers 90-Day Emergency in Babahoyo
events.summary: Severe El Niño-driven flooding has killed 27 people across Ecuador, prompting the city of Babahoyo in Los Ríos province to declare a 90-day flood emergency. Infrastructure damage and displacement are widespread in the lowland agricultural region.

events.headline: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies Passes Contested Fiscal Package Amid Weak Real
events.summary: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved a contested fiscal package by a 353-128 vote, a win for President Lula's government. The real currency traded near a 22-month low as markets weighed the bill's long-term impact on public finances.

events.headline: Russian 'Matryoshka' Disinformation Campaign Targets Spain's Nov 29 Election
events.summary: Researchers say a Russian-linked disinformation operation known as 'Matryoshka' has been running since mid-November to interfere with Spain's upcoming November 29 election. The campaign spreads fabricated narratives to influence voter sentiment ahead of the vote.

events.headline: Armed Group Shuts Libya's Sharara Oilfield, Cutting 350,000 Barrels Per Day
events.summary: An armed group shut down the pipeline at Libya's Sharara oilfield, cutting roughly 350,000 barrels per day of output before the field reopened. The closure highlights the fragility of Libya's oil infrastructure amid ongoing factional disputes.

events.headline: UN's MINURSO Mission in Western Sahara Ends After 35 Years Amid Rising Tensions
events.summary: The United Nations' MINURSO peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ended after 35 years, with the Polisario Front declaring general mobilization in response. Algeria has reportedly killed two more Moroccans at the border, extending a deadly pattern of incidents in 2026.

events.headline: Fiji Declares National State of Disaster, Closes All Schools Over El Niño Drought
events.summary: Fiji declared a national state of disaster and ordered all schools closed nationwide for five days as an El Niño-driven drought crisis deepens across the Pacific. Regional governments are stepping up their response to the worsening water shortage.

events.headline: China Extends Suspension of Rare-Earth Export Curbs on US Through January 2027
events.summary: China extended its suspension of critical-mineral and rare-earth export curbs on the United States through January 2027, maintaining a trade truce agreed by Trump and Xi. The extension provides continued relief to US manufacturers reliant on Chinese rare-earth supplies.

events.headline: Peru's Dengue Cases Surge 238% in 2026 as PAHO Warns of Possible Second Wave
events.summary: Peru reported over 112,000 dengue cases and 148 deaths in 2026, a 238% year-on-year increase, prompting a health emergency declaration in 222 districts. DENV-3 is the predominant strain, and officials warn El Niño conditions could trigger a second wave.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Set Russia's Novoshakhtinsk Oil Refinery Ablaze
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Russia's Rostov region, a major military fuel supplier with 7.5 million tons/year capacity, sparking a large fire. The strike is part of a sustained Ukrainian campaign that has cut Russian crude processing by about 45% since late October.

events.headline: Senegal's Ruling Pastef Party Formally Expels President Faye and 31 Allies
events.summary: Senegal's ruling Pastef party formally expelled President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and 31 other members it deemed 'inactive,' deepening a rupture with Prime Minister-turned-Assembly-Speaker Ousmane Sonko. Faye has launched a rival party amid a budget standoff that threatens IMF aid ahead of the 2027 budget.

events.headline: Zelensky Says He Will Seek New US Aid From Incoming Congress if Trump Peace Push Fails
events.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would pursue a new aid and sanctions package with the incoming Democrat-led US Congress if President Trump's peace initiative does not succeed. The remarks signal Kyiv's effort to hedge against uncertainty in Washington's approach to the war.

events.headline: El Niño-Driven Drought Crisis Deepens Across Southern Africa
events.summary: An El Niño-driven drought is deepening across Southern Africa, straining water and food supplies in multiple countries including Zimbabwe. Regional agencies warn the crisis could worsen food insecurity into 2027 absent coordinated relief efforts.

events.headline: Gunfire Hits Passenger Plane at Port-au-Prince Airport, Grounding Domestic Flights
events.summary: A Sunrise Airways plane was struck by gunfire at Port-au-Prince's airport, prompting the carrier to suspend all domestic flights. The incident underscores persistent gang-related insecurity in Haiti's capital even as a police-backed offensive continues against armed groups.

events.headline: North Korea's Kim Yo-jong Expels Swiss Diplomat, Downgrades Ties
events.summary: North Korean official Kim Yo-jong moved to downgrade relations with Switzerland and expel a Swiss diplomat, linked to a youth camp sanctions dispute tied to the Russia-Ukraine war. The move follows earlier threats to close Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang.

events.headline: Rival Banned Awami League Factions Clash in Gopalganj, Bangladesh, Injuring 20
events.summary: Clashes broke out between rival factions of the banned Awami League in Gopalganj, injuring at least 20 people, four by gunshot or pellet wounds. Six crude bombs were detonated and around 10 shops vandalized, the latest flare-up in political violence spreading across Bangladeshi districts.

events.headline: Japan Confirms Bird Flu Outbreaks in Kyoto and Chiba, Expanding Season's Cases
events.summary: Japan confirmed H5N9 bird flu outbreaks at poultry farms in Kameoka, Kyoto, and in Chiba prefecture, adding to a third outbreak of the season already confirmed at an Aichi egg farm. Authorities have culled affected flocks as part of containment measures.

events.headline: French Prosecutors Probe Alleged Leak of Le Pen Investigation Details to National Rally
events.summary: French prosecutors are investigating whether a senior Interior Ministry prefect, Hugues Moutouh, leaked confidential details of judicial investigations into Marine Le Pen's National Rally party back to the party. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez summoned him; Moutouh denies wrongdoing.

events.headline: ICE Agents Forcibly Remove Father and Daughter From Seattle Airport Jetway
events.summary: ICE officers removed a father and daughter from an Alaska Airlines jetway at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, delaying the flight roughly three hours. The Port of Seattle called the operation 'rogue' and unauthorized, and the incident sparked political backlash.

events.headline: Russian Aircraft Enter South Korea's ADIZ Near Ulleung Island for Third Time in a Week
events.summary: Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's air defense identification zone near Ulleung Island for the third time in a week, briefly prompting a shelter alert. The repeated incursions have raised tensions on the Korean Peninsula amid broader regional security concerns.

events.headline: Peru Declares 60-Day Emergency in 21 Andean Districts After Deadly Earthquakes
events.summary: Peru's government declared a 60-day state of emergency across 21 districts in Huánuco, Junín and Pasco following a magnitude 6.7 earthquake that killed one person and injured 16 in the Junín region. The measure allows expedited relief and infrastructure repair in the affected Andean areas.

events.headline: Police Sergeant Shot in Targeted Ambush on Tasmania's Flinders Island
events.summary: A police sergeant was shot in a targeted ambush outside Whitemark Police Station on Flinders Island, Tasmania. The suspected gunman was later found dead nearby, apparently from return fire, while the sergeant remains hospitalized in serious but stable condition.

events.headline: New Jersey Defends Anti-Mask Law Targeting ICE Agents in Federal Court
events.summary: On Nov. 23, New Jersey urged a federal judge in Camden to reject a Trump administration bid to block the state's law barring law enforcement, including ICE, from wearing masks on duty. New Jersey argued the law has broad exceptions for undercover and tactical operations and has not yet been enforced; the judge did not issue an immediate ruling.

events.headline: Coordinated Bomb Threat Hoaxes Hit Hundreds of Schools in Germany and Denmark
events.summary: Hundreds of schools across multiple German states and parts of Denmark received coordinated emailed bomb threats. Police found no real danger and suspect a hoax or destabilization campaign, part of a wider pattern of similar threats across Europe.

events.headline: Kilmar Abrego Garcia Departs US Voluntarily for Spain After Legal Battle
events.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia departed the United States voluntarily for Spain following a lengthy and high-profile immigration legal battle. His case had drawn national attention over wrongful deportation and due-process disputes.

events.headline: Belgium's 11th Anti-Austerity Strike Shuts Down Both Brussels Airports
events.summary: A national strike against Prime Minister De Wever's austerity budget shut down both Brussels airports, cancelling over 400 flights and affecting more than 50,000 passengers. Only two of Brussels's metro lines remained running during the 11th such strike.

events.headline: Thanksgiving Nor'easter to Bring Damaging Winds, Coastal Flooding to Northeast
events.summary: A developing nor'easter is forecast to move up the East Coast from Nov. 25 into Thanksgiving Day, bringing 40-60 mph wind gusts, moderate-to-major coastal flooding from Virginia to New York, and 1-4 inches of rain. A high wind watch is in effect for New York City and Philadelphia on Thanksgiving, threatening travel for an estimated 81.5 million Americans.

events.headline: Flood Warning Issued for Maricopa and Yuma Counties From Upstream Arizona Dam Release
events.summary: The National Weather Service extended a flood warning for the Gila River covering south-central Maricopa and northeastern Yuma counties, driven by a continuing Army Corps of Engineers release from Painted Rock Dam near Gila Bend that began in October. Several roads and river crossings have been closed, and officials expect elevated flows to continue for roughly another week.

events.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season Ends With Just One Hurricane, a Record Low
events.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season ended with only a single hurricane, marking the latest-ever first hurricane in 121 years of record-keeping. Meteorologists say the unusually quiet season is unlikely to repeat in 2027 given shifting ocean and atmospheric conditions.

events.headline: New Jersey Appellate Court Revives School Segregation Lawsuit
events.summary: On Nov. 23, a New Jersey appellate panel rejected the state's bid to dismiss the long-running Latino Action Network v. New Jersey school segregation lawsuit, allowing it to proceed. The panel stopped short of ruling on whether the state's residency-based policies are unconstitutional; the 2018 suit targets 23 districts where Black and Latino students exceed 90% of enrollment.

events.headline: Egypt and Iraq Sign 11 Cooperation Agreements as PM Al-Zaidi Visits Cairo
events.summary: Egypt and Iraq signed 11 cooperation agreements covering energy and military ties during Iraqi Prime Minister Al-Zaidi's first visit to Cairo. Iraq is also weighing a deal to supply Egypt with up to 10 million barrels of oil.

events.headline: Moldova to Align Sanctions Regime With EU on Russia and Belarus by 2027
events.summary: Moldova announced it will fully align its sanctions regime with the European Union's measures against Russia and Belarus by the end of January 2027. The move is part of Moldova's broader push toward EU integration amid regional security concerns.

events.headline: Côte d'Ivoire Begins Deploying Troops to Haiti's Gang Suppression Force
events.summary: Côte d'Ivoire has started deploying roughly 812 troops, with about 100 already arrived, to join Haiti's Gang Suppression Force in Port-au-Prince and Mirebalais. The reinforcements add to the multinational effort against armed gangs controlling parts of the capital.

events.headline: Nigerian Senate Approves Tinubu's N29.2 Trillion Borrowing Plan for 2026
events.summary: Nigeria's Senate approved President Tinubu's N29.2 trillion borrowing plan for 2026 as part of a revised national budget. The move reflects the government's continued reliance on debt financing amid economic pressures.

events.headline: El Salvador's Dengue Outbreak Grows to Nearly 7,000 Cases, Five Deaths
events.summary: El Salvador's dengue outbreak has reached 6,908 suspected cases and five confirmed deaths, up 31.8% year-on-year, with chikungunya also reappearing. Health authorities continue monitoring the surge as case counts rise through late November.

events.headline: Kiribati Abruptly Evacuates All Residents From Remote Kanton Island
events.summary: Kiribati evacuated all roughly 40-50 residents of remote Kanton Island, a former US military base in the Phoenix Islands, to Tarawa with only about 24 hours' notice. Officials cited El Niño conditions and infrastructure upgrades; residents may not return for up to four years, raising regional unease given past Chinese interest in the island's runway.

events.headline: WHO Chief Visits Cuba, Pledges $2 Million in Vaccines and Medical Equipment
events.summary: WHO Director-General visited Havana and announced $2 million in support for vaccines and medical equipment for Cuba. He also urged the United States to ease fuel sanctions that have hampered the island's healthcare system.

events.headline: Chile Probes Senators' Permits in Forgery Inquiry as Peso Hits 12-Month Low
events.summary: Chilean police visited the Senate as part of a forgery investigation into senators' permits, adding political uncertainty. Separately, Chile's peso fell to a 12-month low amid a slide in copper prices, the country's key export commodity.

events.headline: Magnitude 5.3 Earthquake Strikes Nepal's Koshi Province, Felt in India
events.summary: A magnitude 5.3 earthquake struck Nepal's Koshi Province near Phaktanglung, with tremors felt across parts of eastern India. No major damage or casualties were immediately reported.
